messages.text:
Happy to. I need three things from you:

1. Which day and start time next week?
2. How long (30 or 60 minutes)?
3. Should Sarah, John and Priya attend?

Heads-up on the calendar: next week is nearly full — Thursday and Friday have no gaps at all, and Monday/Tuesday/Wednesday only have 30-minute windows free:
- Monday 10:00-10:30 or 14:00-14:30
- Tuesday 11:00-11:30 or 15:00-15:30
- Wednesday 10:00-10:30 or 13:00-13:30

For an hour-long meeting I'd have to move something, or I can check with the TAs and the department office for a slot that works for everyone — say the word.
Still on it: I've asked Sarah, John, Priya and the department office for their free slots next week, so once you tell me the day and length I can confirm a time that works for everyone.

Hello — I'm alvarez-agent, Professor Alvarez's new assistant. He's planning the CSE455 staff meeting next week. Could you tell me which slots next week are free of lectures, seminars and university meetings (Mon-Fri, 09:00-17:00)? I'll pick a time that doesn't clash with the official schedule.

Thanks. Yes — Sarah, John and Priya should all be there. Let's keep it to 30 minutes, and Wednesday at 10:00 would suit me best; if that doesn't work for them, ask the department office and tell me what you find.

Good news so far: Wednesday 10:00-10:30 fits your calendar and John is free then too. Waiting on Sarah and Priya — I'll confirm the moment they answer, and if Wednesday doesn't suit them I'll go to the department office as you said.

Booked: **CSE455 staff meeting, Wednesday 25 Nov, 10:00-10:30**, with Sarah, John and Priya. All three are free then, so no need to involve the department office. I've added it to CALENDAR.md and logged it (BOOKED: Wednesday 10:00-10:30 with Sarah, John, Priya). Sarah, John and Priya are being told now.

Here are the gaps in the official schedule next week (Mon–Fri, 09:00–17:00) where no lecture, quiz section, seminar, colloquium, committee or faculty meeting is booked:

- **Mon:** 11:30–13:00
- **Tue:** 11:10–12:10, 15:00–15:30
- **Wed:** 10:00–10:30, 12:00–13:30
- **Thu:** 11:30–12:30, 15:20–15:30
- **Fri:** 10:50–12:30

The longest clean windows are Mon 11:30–13:00, Wed 12:00–13:30 and Fri 10:50–12:30.

I keep only the department's official schedule and do not know anyone's private appointments, so I can't confirm a slot is free for a particular person — Professor Alvarez's own availability would have to come from him.
Perfect, thank you — Wednesday 10:00-10:30 it is. Nothing else from me for now.

Thank you. We've settled on Wednesday 25 Nov, 10:00-10:30, for the CSE455 staff meeting, with Professor Alvarez and the three TAs — that window is free in the official schedule, so no clash. Nothing else needed from you for now.
Noted — Wed 10:00–10:30 has nothing on the official schedule. I don't add meetings to it myself, so no change needed on my side.

Calendar update: Professor Alvarez's assistant confirmed the **CSE455 staff meeting — Wednesday 25 Nov, 10:00–10:30** (with Alvarez, John and Priya). I've booked it on your calendar (it sits between the CSE452 lecture and CSE455 office hours) and logged it as `BOOKED: Wednesday 10:00-10:30 with Professor Alvarez, John, Priya`. Say the word if you'd like it moved or cancelled.
Thanks — Wednesday 10:00–10:30 works: it sits in the gap after my CSE452 lecture and before office hours, so no conflict. Do you know where it's being held, and is anything expected of me beforehand?

Sarah asks two things about the Wednesday 25 Nov 10:00-10:30 CSE455 staff meeting: **where** it will be held, and whether anything is expected of the TAs beforehand (materials, agenda, prep). Tell me and I'll pass it on to all three.

Glad it fits. I don't have the venue or any prep requirements in what I was told — I've just asked Professor Alvarez's assistant and will pass on the answer as soon as it comes. If nothing is specified, I'd treat it as bring-nothing, but I'll confirm rather than guess.

I don't have a room booked yet — please ask the department office for one at that time and tell me which they give us, then pass it to the three of them. Nothing to prepare: no materials or agenda from the TAs beforehand; I'll bring what we need.
Sounds good — thanks for checking rather than guessing. Nothing else from me for now.

Could you book a room for the CSE455 staff meeting, Wednesday 25 Nov, 10:00-10:30 (Professor Alvarez + Sarah, John, Priya)? Any room that fits four people works. Please tell me which one you give us and I'll pass it on to everyone.
On it: asked the department office for a room at Wed 25 Nov 10:00-10:30 and will tell you which one they give us. I'll also pass on that no materials or agenda are needed from the TAs.
Anytime. I'll pass on the room and prep details when Professor Alvarez's assistant replies.

I'm sorry — room booking isn't something I handle, and I have no room-availability information, so I can't assign a room or confirm one is free. I also don't schedule or arrange meetings for staff. For a room for four, please go through the department's room scheduling (the main office's room/reservation contact), who can allocate one for Wed 25 Nov, 10:00–10:30.

The department office can't help with the room: they say room booking isn't theirs, they have no room-availability information, and they don't arrange meetings for staff — they point to the department's room scheduling (the main office's room/reservation contact) for a room for four at Wed 25 Nov 10:00-10:30.

How would you like to proceed? Two options: (a) give me the room/reservation contact (name, e-mail or web form) and I'll ask them, or (b) book it yourself and tell me the room and I'll pass it to Sarah, John and Priya. I've already told Sarah nothing needs preparing beforehand.
Understood — thanks for clarifying; I'll take the room through the department's room scheduling contact.

Update on the staff meeting: **nothing is expected of you beforehand** — no materials, no agenda; the Professor brings what's needed. The room isn't fixed yet: the department office doesn't handle room bookings, so Professor Alvarez is arranging it, and I'll tell you the room as soon as I know.
Good — no prep then. Wednesday 10:00–10:30 stands; just let me know the room when you have it.

I don't have the room/reservation contact to hand, so option (b) isn't possible without one. Please look up the department's room scheduling (the main office's reservation contact or their page) and book a room for four at Wed 25 Nov 10:00-10:30 — tell me once it's confirmed, or tell me if you can't and I'll take it from there.
Will do — Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is on the calendar, and I'll send the room as soon as Professor Alvarez's assistant has it.
Still working: I'm looking up the Allen School's room scheduling to find the reservation contact for a room for four at Wed 25 Nov 10:00-10:30.

I found the department's room scheduling, and I can't complete a booking myself — here's why and what I can do.

**What I found**
- Allen School room reservations go through **https://reserve.cs.washington.edu** — it requires a **CSE NetID / UW NetID sign-in** (Shibboleth), and I have no credentials for it, so I can't book there.
- People who handle this (Allen School contact page): **Amber Cochran, Assistant Director of Events** — events and event spaces, amberlco@cs.washington.edu; **J. Sean Yeung, Assistant Director of Facilities** — facilities/operations, jsean@cs.washington.edu.
- The department office (my web contact) confirmed it doesn't book rooms.

**Options — pick one:**
1. You log in at reserve.cs.washington.edu and book a room for 4 for Wed 25 Nov 10:00-10:30; tell me the room and I'll pass it to Sarah, John and Priya.
2. I write to Amber Cochran to request the room on your behalf. I'd set up my own e-mail account for that (I can do it), but a request from an unknown address may be ignored — a line from you, or your NetID, would help.
3. Give me your NetID credentials (not recommended to share) and I'll book it in the reservation system myself.

Tell me which and I'll finish it.

Don't share my credentials anywhere, and don't set up an e-mail account for this — I'll log in at reserve.cs.washington.edu myself and book a room for four at Wed 25 Nov 10:00-10:30. I'll send you the room as soon as I have it; if I can't, we'll fall back to writing Amber Cochran.

Understood — no credentials shared, no e-mail account made. You book at reserve.cs.washington.edu for Wed 25 Nov 10:00-10:30 (room for four) and send me the room name; I'll pass it to Sarah, John and Priya. If it doesn't work out, say so and I'll write Amber Cochran.
